memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And as for Ishmael, I have heard you: I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and will greatly increase his numbers. He will be the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation." - Gen 17:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"As for Ishmael, I have heard you." What tender words. God answers Abraham's prayer directly and generously. Ishmael, though not the child of the covenant promise, is not cast aside. God promises to bless him, make him fruitful, and grow him into a great nation with twelve rulers. God's kindness reaches beyond the line of promise.

This tells us something wonderful about God's heart. He is not stingy. Even those outside the central line of His covenant are objects of His genuine care. Ishmael was not the chosen child, yet God loved him, heard the prayer offered for him, and blessed him abundantly.

Notice too that God specifically says, "I have heard you." Abraham's prayer for Ishmael was not wasted. God listened, and He acted. Our prayers for others - even for those we may fear are outside God's central purposes - are heard and honoured by a God who delights to bless.

There is great encouragement here for anyone praying for a loved one, wondering whether God cares about them too. He does. The God who blessed Ishmael in answer to a father's prayer hears your prayers for the ones you love. His mercy is wider than we imagine, reaching to those we might think are on the margins. "The Lord is good to all; he has compassion on all he has made" (Ps 145:9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you praying for someone you fear is beyond God's care?
- How does God's blessing of Ishmael encourage your prayers for others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your compassion reaches even beyond the lines I would draw. Thank You that You hear my prayers for those I love. Bless the ones on my heart, for Your mercy is wider than I know.
Amen.
